definition: The change in the observed frequency of a wave (and, for a moving source or for light, its wavelength) when the source and the observer move towards or away from each other: higher when they approach, lower when they move apart.

An increase in the observed wavelength (and decrease in frequency) of light from a source moving away from the observer; for speeds much less than $c$, $\frac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda} \approx \frac{v}{c}$.
